{{nihongo|'''Amayukawata Shrine'''|天湯川田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kawachi Province]].

'''Amayukawata Shrine''' (あまゆかわたじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Takaida, {{ill|Kashiwara|ar|كاشيوارا (أوساكا)|ca|Kashiwara|ce|Касивара|ceb|Kashiwara-shi|de|Kashiwara|eo|Kaŝiŭara|es|Kashiwara (Osaka)|et|Kashiwara|fa|کاشی‌وارا، اوساکا|fi|Kashiwara|fr|Kashiwara|gl|Kashiwara|hy|Կաշիվարա|it|Kashiwara|ja|柏原市|ko|가시와라시|mg|Kashihara|mzn|کاشی‌وارا، اوساکا|nl|Kashiwara|pl|Kashiwara|pt|Kashiwara|ro|Kashiwara|ru|Касивара|sv|Kashiwara|tg|Кашивара|th|คาชิวาระ|tl|Kashiwara|tr|Kashiwara|tt|Касивара|uk|Кашівара|ur|کاشیوارا|vi|Kashiwara, Ōsaka|war|Kashiwara, Osaka|zh|柏原市|zh_classical|柏原市|zh_min_nan|Kasiwara-chhī|zh_yue|柏原|qid=Q873583}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking system}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is enshrined on the site of the pagoda ruins of {{ill|Tosaka-dera|Q92453846|qid=Q92453846|lt=Torisaka-dera}}, one of the {{ill|Kawachi Six Temples|Q21652904|qid=Q21652904}} visited by Emperors Shōmu and Kōken during the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}. The shrine grounds are maintained as Kashiwara City Takaida Park.

=== Enshrined deities ===
The shrine enshrines three deities: {{ill|Ame-no-Yukawata|Q52319907|qid=Q52319907|lt=Amayukawa-geta no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|fr|Ama-no-Koyane-no-mikoto|it|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋命|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯀꯣꯌꯅꯦ|pt|Ame-no-Koyane|ru|Амэ-но коянэ-но микото|simple|Ame-no-Koyane|zh|天兒屋命|qid=Q2564508|lt=Amenokoyane no Mikoto}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi no Mikoto}}. Among these, Amayukawa-geta no Mikoto is regarded as the ancestral deity of the ancient Toritori no Muraji clan that ruled the surrounding area.

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown, but Torisaka-dera, said to have stood on the shrine grounds, was the clan temple of the Toritori clan. In the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}, there are entries for Torisaka Village and Toritori Village in {{ill|Ōgata district|ja|大県郡|zh|大縣郡|qid=Q11438107}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}}, suggesting that together with the nearby {{ill|Sukunakawata Shrine|ja|宿奈川田神社|qid=Q11455616}}, the Toritori no Muraji clan enshrined their ancestral deity here. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as “Amayukawata Shrine, Ōagata District, Kawachi Province” and ranked as a minor shrine.

From the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} through the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}, it was known by names such as “Kawata Daimyōjin,” “Ōmiya Daimyōjin,” and “Kasuga Shrine,” but in Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|ab|1872|af|1872|als|1872|am|1872 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1872|ar|1872|ary|1872|arz|1872|ast|1872|avk|1872|az|1872|azb|۱۸۷۲ (میلادی)|ba|1872 йыл|ban|1872|bar|1872|bat_smg|1872|bcl|1872|be|1872|be_x_old|1872|bg|1872|bn|১৮৭২|bpy|মারি ১৮৭২|br|1872|bs|1872.|ca|1872|cdo|1872 nièng|ce|1872 шо|ceb|1872|ckb|١٨٧٢|crh|1872|cs|1872|csb|1872|cv|1872|cy|1872|da|1872|de|1872|diq|1872|el|1872|eml|1872|eo|1872|es|1872|et|1872|eu|1872|fa|۱۸۷۲|fi|1872|fiu_vro|1872|fo|1872|fr|1872|frp|1872|frr|1872|fur|1872|fy|1872|ga|1872|gan|1872年|gcr|1872|gd|1872|gl|1872|gv|1872|he|1872|hi|१८७२|hif|1872|hr|1872.|hsb|1872|ht|1872 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1872|hy|1872|hyw|1872 թուական|ia|1872|id|1872|ilo|1872|io|1872|is|1872|it|1872|ja|1872年|jv|1872|ka|1872|kaa|1872|kk|1872 жыл|kn|೧೮೭೨|ko|1872년|krc|1872 джыл|ku|1872|kv|1872-ӧд во|la|1872|lb|1872|lez|1872 йис|li|1872|lij|1872|lmo|1872|lt|1872 m.|lv|1872. gads|mai|१८७२|map_bms|1872|mdf|1872|mg|1872|mhr|1872|mi|1872|min|1872|mk|1872|mr|इ.स. १८७२|mrj|1872 и|ms|1872|my|၁၈၇၂|myv|1872 ие|mzn|۱۸۷۲|nah|1872|nap|1872|nds|1872|nds_nl|1872|new|ई सं १८७२|nl|1872|nn|1872|no|1872|nrm|1872|nso|1872|oc|1872|olo|1872|or|୧୮୭୨|os|1872-æм аз|pa|1872|pam|1872|pl|1872|pnb|1872|pt|1872|qu|1872|ro|1872|ru|1872 год|rue|1872|sa|१८७२|sah|1872|scn|1872|sd|1872ع|se|1872|sh|1872.|shn|1872|si|1872|simple|1872|sk|1872|sl|1872|smn|1872|sq|1872|sr|1872|stq|1872|su|1872|sv|1872|sw|1872|szl|1872|ta|1872|te|1872|tet|1872|tg|Соли 1872|th|พ.ศ. 2415|tk|1872|tl|1872|tly|1872|tr|1872|tt|1872 ел|udm|1872 ар|uk|1872|ur|1872ء|uz|1872|vec|1872|vi|1872|vls|1872|vo|1872|wa|1872|war|1872|xmf|1872|yi|1872|za|1872 nienz|zea|1872|zh|1872年|zh_classical|一八七二年|zh_min_nan|1872 nî|zh_yue|1872年|qid=Q7753}}) it was renamed to its present name and designated a village shrine.

=== Shrine grounds ===
The grounds are currently maintained as “Kashiwara City Takaida Park,” with the shrine buildings standing together at the top of a hill within the park.

=== Torisaka-dera Pagoda Ruins ===
Within the grounds are remains of the ancient temple {{ill|Tosaka-dera|Q92453846|qid=Q92453846|lt=Torisaka-dera}}. Excavations conducted in Shōwa 36 ({{ill|1961|Q3696|qid=Q3696}}) uncovered the pagoda’s central foundation stone and rainwater drainage ditches. The central foundation stone is an underground-style foundation embedded deeper than the podium surface, made of granite measuring 1.2 m on each side and 63 cm thick. The pillar hole has a conical reliquary cavity with a diameter of 50.5 cm at the base and a depth of 15.5 cm. Observation of the soil layers revealed that the central pillar was wrapped in clay and then backfilled in alternating layers of charcoal and soil mixed with small stones. Based on the size of the pillar hole and the distance between the foundation stone and the drainage ditches, the pagoda is estimated to have been a three-story pagoda approximately 20 m tall, constructed in the mid to late 7th century.
